title: Kirby's classical repertoire, Sunday broadcasts and heavy schedule
summary: He agrees the classics were chosen partly for ASCAP public domain reasons; the band did a Sunday sustaining radio program with little rehearsal, a record date and a transcription session every month.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Now, you have said you believe the reason Kirby played so many of the classics was because of an ASCAP thing to do with public domain.

Yes. That's true. Yes. Then we had a sustaining program. We broadcast every Sunday around -- I think it was 12:00 or 1:00 o'clock on Sunday afternoon. And of course it required a lot of music, you know. Every Sunday was a different program. And the band wasn't -- wasn't very old then. I would say it was a year old, if that old. So everything was tense and, you know, and you had to be -- you had to give 150 percent every Sunday, and we didn't have much time to rehearse or anything like that. I think at that time they allowed a half-hour rehearsal, and we had to get
You did a lot of things with Langworth too, transcriptions.

Oh, yes. We had a transcription date every month. We were working at the Onyx Club, we had a record date every month, we had this transcription every month, which for those days was as much as any group in our position, I'd say, you know, could have done. We had the commercial and the job at the Onyx Club and the transcription, a month. So it all -- and we were working real hard. We really worked hard.
And that's why it was a very tight group.
